title: Intermittent packet loss
symptom: Calls and apps keep freezing for a few seconds, suggesting packet loss
user_description: My video calls freeze every few minutes and the accounting app sometimes says connection lost. Then it comes back. It's been like this all week.

options.text: Run a continuous ping (ping -t) to the gateway and beyond to see where the loss starts, try another cable and port, note the times, and escalate if the problem is beyond the desk
options.why: Pinging step by step shows where packets go missing. Swapping the cable and port rules out the desk, and the timings help the network team.

options.text: Restart his PC every time it freezes
options.why: Does not find the cause and loses work.
The apps work when the network does. The drops come from the connection.

options.text: Tell him to stop using video calls
options.why: Avoids the problem instead of fixing it.

hints: Is the problem on the PC, the desk cable, or further away?
How can you see packets going missing?
What information would help the network team?
real_world_tip: Ping the gateway first, then something further like a company server. If the loss already shows to the gateway, the problem is close to the desk.

escalation.team_why: Loss beyond the desk comes from switches, links or other network kit that the network team manages.

details.text: Ping results showing where the loss starts
details.why: Shows them exactly which part of the path is dropping packets.
Lets them match the drops to switch logs or busy periods.

details.text: What you already tried (another cable and port)
details.why: Rules out the desk, so they do not repeat it.

details.text: Ask them to restart the main switch right now
details.why: Cuts off the whole office during work hours. Let the network team decide how to fix it.
Not needed, and passwords are never shared.
